chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Two just persons from among you, or two others from among others than you.' He said: 'Those from among you are Muslims, and those from among others than you are from the People of the Book.'

He said: 'That is only when a Muslim man dies in a land of strangers, so he seeks two Muslim men to bear witness to his bequest. But if he cannot find two Muslims, let him have two men from the People of the Book, who are acceptable among their own companions, bear witness to his bequest.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'two just persons' mentioned in Quran 5:106 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential application of Quran 5:106, establishing a hierarchical protocol for witnesses in bequests where a Muslim dies in a foreign land (ghurba) without access to Muslim witnesses. It clarifies that 'from among you' denotes Muslims, while 'others than you' refers to the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), specifically allowing two trustworthy non-Muslims to validate the will when Muslim witnesses are unavailable. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical adaptability in legal testimony while maintaining the primacy of Muslim witnesses.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Hamza Bin Humran, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:106] two just persons from among you, or two others from among others than you. So heasws said: ‘Those from among you are the Muslims, and those from among others than you are from people of the Book.

But rather, that is when the Muslim man dies in a land of strangers, so he seeks two Muslim men to bear witness his bequest. But if he cannot find two Muslims, so let two men bear witness upon his bequest, the ones under the responsibility (Ahl Al-Zimma) from the people of the Book, both of whom are acceptable among their own companions’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from Jamil ibn Salih from Hamzah ibn Humran who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . two just man from among you or two men from other people. 5 [5:106]
He (the Imam) said, ‘The ‘two from you’ means two Muslims, the ‘two from other people 5 means from the followers of the book. 5

He (the Imam) then said, ‘This can happen when a Muslim dies far away from his land where he cannot find two Muslim men, thus he can appoint two taxpayers of the followers of the book who are acceptable among their own people to bear witness to his will."
